newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rates end higher ahead of elections.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rates end higher ahead of elections.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed 70 basis points higher at 20.60 percent on Thursday, amid tight liquidity and uneasiness ahead of Sunday's elections, dealers said.
"Rates closed under a little pressure due to the elections and the central bank cutoff, but apart from that, the market was very quiet," a trader said.
Next Wednesday is the monthly deadline for banks to settle balances outstanding on checking accounts held with the central bank.

Mexicans go to the polls on Sunday to elect all members of the lower house of Congress, a quarter of the Senate, six state governors and, for the first time, a mayor of Mexico City. Previously, a presidential appointee held that post.

The outcome of the mayoral race is critical, because for the first time President Ernesto Zedillo's Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) may lose control of the country's nerve center to an opposition party. The PRI has ruled Mexico for the past 68 years.
Despite the possibility of a political shift, fixed-income analysts said investors were only moderately apprehensive ahead of the elections.
Dealers said secondary rates also gained as foreign investment flooded into the Mexican bourse, with IPC blue-chip index closing up 32.39 points to a record 4,591.62.
Banco de Mexico drained 4.287 billion pesos from the money market through three direct sales of paper and six repos.
Overnight rates on bank paper ended up 10 basis points at 21.60 percent.
Liquidity of 1.301 billion pesos was due to return to the system on Friday from prior central bank participation.
